en:
...Something about this feels wrong, doesn't it?
The people who told their stories just disappearing like that.
Iwashita and Kazama are already gone.
...And now it's my turn to talk, is it?{p}

Let me start by introducing myself.
I'm Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
...Pleased to meet you.
Have any of you ever seen a suicide?
I have, you know.
Someone jumping to their death.
And twice, no less.{p}

The first time, the person had already jumped.
It seems they jumped from dozens of meters up, and there was nothing left of their original shape.
You know how sometimes a dog or cat that got run over by a car just gets left lying there, never cleared away?
Haven't you ever seen one?
Those are almost cute by comparison.
You couldn't tell whether it was a person or just a lump of meat.
Blood and bits of flesh were splattered over a pretty wide area.
The people who saw it turned their faces away, going 'Ugh, how awful,' and yet every one of them kept looking out of the corner of their eye as they walked past.
Humans are strange creatures, aren't they?{p}

The second time, I saw the very moment of the jump.
It was from the third floor of a small building.
Apparently it came out of a lovers' quarrel that got out of hand.
It was a woman who jumped.
With that type, you never know whether they really meant to die.
I'm sure she only meant to scare the man.
But things had gone too far, and she couldn't back down...
That's how it looked.
At the moment she jumped, she had a face like a demon's.
So a human face can turn into something like that.
That was the first time I learned it.
...She was alive.
After she hit the ground she lay there without moving, but you could hear her groaning.
I'll never forget that groaning.
I've never heard a voice that stuck in my ears like that one.
She was in real agony.
And there was bone sticking out of her leg.
The blood wasn't as red as I'd expected.
Thinking back now, I feel like it was cherry-blossom pink.
That's how it looked to my eyes.
Maybe the blood soaked into the bone was what made it look that color.{p}

And apparently, when you jump, it wrecks your internal organs.
At the moment you hit the ground, the organs can't withstand the shock and the pressure.
So even if you survive, in a lot of cases you end up with damage to your organs.
I'm not a doctor, though, so I can't tell you whether that's true or not.
...By the way, do you know what sound a jumper makes?
The sound at the instant a body slams into the ground.
You know those sheets of corrugated tin?
The thin sheets, the wavy kind.
Well, you lay one of those on soft ground.
Then you take a stone like a pickling stone, big enough that you have to hold it in both arms, and drop it from about chest height.
They say the sound it makes is exactly like a person slamming into the ground.
A fairly heavy, dull sound, wouldn't you say?
The human body looks pretty soft, doesn't it?
But apparently, when it slams into the ground, it's as if the hard bones hit it directly.
Actually, when I saw it, there wasn't much of a dull sound.
I think it was a drier sound.
Maybe you have to fall from somewhere higher to get that kind of dull sound.{p}

For instance, I wonder what sound it would make if someone jumped off the roof of the new school building.
It's the roof of a four-story building.
If someone fell from that height, would they survive?
Or would they die instantly?{p}Which do you think it would be?
I don't think they'd die instantly
I think they'd die instantly
There's no way I could know that

...I see.
So that's what you think.{p}

Actually, there was a student who tested it, a long time ago.
It wasn't that he was unhappy with school or his private life, or that he had anything troubling him.
He got along fine with his friends, too.
He just couldn't stop wondering what would happen to someone who fell to their death from that height.
Whenever he thought about it, it nagged at him and nagged at him, until he simply had to find out.
Do you think that's strange?
But I understand how he felt.{p}

Haven't you ever been holding a needle or something and thought, 'It would really hurt if I jabbed this under my fingernail'?
When you're deep-frying something, haven't you ever thought, 'What would happen if I plunged my hand into this oil'?
Don't people have moments when they just can't help tormenting themselves?
And then they imagine it actually happening and get a little shiver of excitement.
I do that sort of thing, you know.{p}What about you? Don't you?
Yes, I do
No, I don't

...I see.
So you don't.
Then maybe I'm the abnormal one after all.
But I believe that every human being has a moment when they think things like that.
I think that's what human weakness is.{p}

So the boy who got curious about the school roof... maybe he just happened to have those self-destructive moments one after another, don't you think?
The boy's name was Nobuhiko Aizawa.
From what I hear, he was a truly ordinary person in every way.
That's exactly why I think so.
"Hey, if you jumped off the roof of this building, do you think you'd survive?"
"Nobuhiko. Have you gone screwy in the head or something?
Where'd that come from all of a sudden?"
When he asked his friends about it, that's what they said, and they laughed at him.
The more seriously Aizawa said it, the funnier his friends thought the joke was, and they laughed even harder.
Aizawa was an ordinary person, after all.
He didn't press them any further; when his friends laughed, he laughed right along with them.{p}

Even so, whenever he was alone, he agonized over it.
He didn't know why it bothered him so much, and he even wondered whether he himself had gone strange.
Still, the only way to settle it was to actually find out.
Jump himself...
Or push somebody else off.
Every time the thought came to him, he told himself he mustn't think such stupid things. But the harder you hold back, the less you can contain a desire.
And the stronger the desire, the truer that is.
As day followed day, the desire grew with them, and it was only a matter of time before it broke through the shell of reason that held it down.{p}

He started keeping a notebook.
In the notebook he scrawled, in no particular order, the names of people connected to the school, starting with his classmates.
Upperclassmen, underclassmen, even teachers.
He had begun choosing who should be pushed off the roof.
And at the top of that list was his own name.
Perhaps that was the last scrap of reason he had left.{p}

The desire had grown to its full size.
And he made up his mind to take the step that must never be taken.{p}The problem was: who would be the victim of the experiment?
The moment he thought that, perhaps the devil already had him under its spell.
Himself
A teacher he didn't like
A student he didn't like

There weren't really any students he didn't like.
He got along reasonably well with everyone, and by nature he just couldn't bring himself to dislike people.
So he thought it over.
Every school has its delinquents.
At his school, too, plenty of students had suffered at their hands.
If he pushed one of the delinquents off the roof, then even if he died, more people would be glad than not.
That's what Aizawa told himself.
He told himself that to justify, even a little, what he was about to do.
The target was decided.
Tatsuya Kuwahata, one of a gang of delinquents.{p}

He hurriedly worked out a plan and put it into action right away.
He was dying to carry it out as soon as he possibly could.
Luring a delinquent out was easy.
He said there was a guy he wanted roughed up, and he'd pay for it.
Kuwahata took the bait immediately.
...Never dreaming that he would soon be pushed off the roof.
Then, when Kuwahata came up to the roof, Aizawa watched for an opening and made him breathe in the chloroform he had prepared in advance.
Kuwahata went limp at once, before he could even struggle.{p}

Trembling with excitement that his wish would soon come true, Aizawa dragged Kuwahata's body across the roof to the edge.
There was a railing around the roof, but it wasn't very high.{p}

Then he hoisted Kuwahata onto his shoulder, leaned out over the railing, and peered down.
It was only a little over ten meters above the ground, but it still made his head spin.
Now that he was actually facing it, Aizawa felt a moment of hesitation.{p}Was it really all right to go through with this?
Drop Kuwahata
Think better of it
Jump himself after all

He had come this far.
If he didn't do it now and Kuwahata figured it out later, there was no telling what would happen to him.
Besides, the guy was hated by everyone, wasn't he?
Telling himself the world would be better off without him, Aizawa finally pushed Kuwahata off the roof.{p}

Maybe because he was unconscious, he fell like a mannequin, hit the ground, and lay there without moving.
"......I can't really tell from up here."{p}

Aizawa ran down the stairs as fast as he could to see whether Kuwahata was alive or dead.
It was after school and the place was deserted, so luckily no one came crowding around or raised an alarm.{p}
Relieved, Aizawa slept soundly that night for the first time in a very long while.{p}Do you think Kuwahata really died?
I think he died
He was actually alive

The next day at school, everyone was talking about Kuwahata.
His death had been settled as a suicide.
Kuwahata had always been a problem student, so no one looked too deeply into the cause.
For a while after that, Aizawa got to enjoy a wonderfully carefree school life.
...But it lasted only a short time.
As time went on, a problem cropped up again.{p}

Maybe Kuwahata had died back then because he'd been unconscious.
If he hadn't been made to breathe the chloroform, maybe he wouldn't have died...?
When he thought that, he couldn't stop himself from checking again.
Hah, there are still plenty of delinquents.
Push two or three more off and nobody'll be any worse off.
Aizawa thought such things with a smirk; by now there wasn't the slightest trace of guilt left in him.{p}

The next day, the second experiment was carried out.
This time, he called out a delinquent, hit him from behind with a bat, and pushed him off while he was weakened.
"...Just as I thought.
Dead again."
This time the head had split open and its contents had spilled out; one look was enough to tell he was dead.{p}

And once again, the school wrote it off as a suicide.
Even so, his satisfaction lasted only an instant.
This time, maybe he'd died because of the blow from the bat.
When he thought that, he couldn't stop himself from testing another method.
And so he did it again.{p}

This time, after knocking his victim out with chloroform, he tied his hands and feet, waited for him to wake up, and then pushed him off.
"...Dead again.
So they do die after all."
This time, surely, he would be satisfied.
Aizawa was certain of it.
But satisfaction never came.
That might have been just a fluke.
Maybe people don't really die.
A human being couldn't die that easily.
When he thought that, he wanted to run the experiment again so badly he couldn't sit still.{p}

That only sent Aizawa's desire soaring even higher.
He was dying to run the experiment one more time somehow, even if he had to sneak into the school in the middle of the night.
But the delinquents seemed to be frightened; no matter how smoothly Aizawa tried to talk them into it, none of them would take the bait.
The wolves had had their fangs pulled and had become as meek as puppies.
That fanned the flames of his desire even higher.
And at last, Aizawa decided to sink his venomous fangs into one of his close friends.{p}

"...There's something I need to talk to you about.
Sorry, but would you hear me out?"
With that, he lured one of his friends out to a park in the middle of the night.{p}The problem was what to do after that.
Knock the friend out with chloroform
Beat the friend with a bat
Strangle the friend to death right there

Aizawa stuffed the guinea pig into a burlap sack he had prepared in advance and carried it on his back to the school.
Then he snuck into the school at night and silently made his way up to the roof.
Of course, the door was locked.
He broke the lock with pliers and a hammer, and the wind came gusting in; he met it head-on with his whole body.{p}

Who knew the school at night could feel this good?
Thinking that, he took a deep breath and dragged the sack out after him.
"...This is my first time at school at night."
Aizawa tossed the sack down in a corner of the roof and for a while enjoyed the night view from up there.{p}
After indulging in such thoughts for a while, he finally set about the experiment.{p}

But then...
The sack lay there flat, like it had lost all its air!
While he'd been lost in the night view, the guinea pig had come to and escaped.
"Aaaaaaaaaagh!"
Aizawa screamed in frustration and grief.{p}

When he looked, he could see something like an ant running across the schoolyard.
It was the guinea pig that had escaped from the sack.
Even if he chased after it now, there was no way he would catch up.
Just then, mixed in with the wind, Aizawa heard someone's voice calling.{p}

When he happened to look down, the earth was beckoning to him.
He even had the illusion that it was opening its huge mouth wide, waiting for its prey to fall.
After all, the soil down there had sucked up the blood of three people.
It would be no wonder at all if it had acquired a taste for blood.
Aizawa put his hand on the railing.{p}Then he leaned out even further and stared at the waiting ground.
Jump
Think better of it

There was no escaping it anymore.
"I have to do the experiment, no matter what..."{p}
Muttering as if possessed, Aizawa threw himself off, his eyes wide open.{p}

The next day, the school was in an uproar.
The friend who had escaped from Aizawa had confessed everything.{p}

'Dad, Mom, and everyone.
I am going to be eaten by the monster that lives on the roof.
If I do not become its sacrifice, there will be more and more victims.
I am setting off on a journey. Goodbye.'{p}

The police concluded that he had run away from home.
And a search party was organized.
But he was never found.
Do you understand why they did that?
Aizawa's body was never found.
Aizawa was supposed to have jumped from the roof, yet not only was there no body, there wasn't a single trace of him.
If it had been found, the police might have interpreted things differently.{p}

Was Aizawa really eaten by the monster that's said to live on the roof?
Or did he never jump at all, and set off on a journey somewhere?{p}

...To tell you the truth, I know, you see.
Where Aizawa is.{p}Would you like to know?
I want to know
I don't want to know
I'm not particularly interested

I see.
The truth is, Aizawa is still on the roof, even now.{p}

What?
You've been up on the roof, but there was nobody like that?
Hm hm hm... Well, of course not.
You can't see Aizawa under ordinary circumstances.
If you like, shall I let you meet him?
What do you say?{p}Why don't we all go up to the roof together, right now?
Go up
Don't go up

Well then, let's go.
...I do think the story that a monster lives in this school is true.
I can't shake the feeling, myself, of being possessed by something.
No, I don't mean me.
I mean all of you at this school.
Though I suppose that includes me, too.{p}

Feels nice, doesn't it?
The summer wind is warm and muggy, and truly pleasant.
Come, {a}{f:.|.}
Why don't you try it too?
Look down from this roof.
From barely a dozen meters up, people already look like ants, don't they?
Wouldn't you like to give yourself to this school as well?
What do you say?
Wouldn't you like to be free of it all?
Wouldn't you like to set off on a journey?{p}Just like Aizawa did...
I'll set off on a journey
I have no intention of setting off on any journey

...I see.
Perhaps it's still too early for you.{p}

Oh yes, I promised to let you meet Aizawa.
Meeting Aizawa is easy, you know.
You just say this:
"Aizawa, let's begin the experiment."{p}Simple, isn't it?
Say those words
Say nothing

"So if I say it, I'll get to meet him?"
{f:I|I} asked in return.{p}

Arai's eyes looked as if they were gazing at something far away.
The three who hadn't told their stories yet silently watched the exchange between Arai and {f:me|me}.
"Arai.
May I ask you one thing?
What is it that's in this school?
What are you saying everyone is possessed by?"{p}

Arai gave a broad smile.
"Say it, please. Say those words.
Then you might understand."
It was true: something was in this school.
{f:I|I} {f:had sensed it myself|could sense it too}.
{f:I|I} nodded at Arai's words.
And then... I said it.
"Aizawa.
Let's begin the experiment!"
It happened in that very instant.{p}

"Look out!"
Before {f:I|I} could even reach out, Arai's body was flying through the air.{p}

"Ah!"
A huge skull, so vast it covered the whole sky, was floating up there.
{f:Was that|Could that be} what Arai had pointed at?
"...Is that Aizawa?"{p}

The skull vanished in an instant.
Before I knew it, the three who were left had gathered around {f:me|me}.
"What now? Three of 'em have vanished on us.
You still gonna keep this going?"
One of them asked.
What should I do?
I never dreamed it would come to this.
Maybe I could still turn back now.
If I kept on like this, I felt I'd only sink in deeper...
I couldn't shake that feeling.
Was what was happening around {f:me|me} right now real...
Or was it an illusion...{p}Should I really keep going like this{f:?|?}
Continue
Stop

"Let's do it.
...If it's all right with all of you.
I feel like we can't let it end like this."
The three nodded in silence.{p}

And so {f:we|we} left the roof and {f:went back|decided to go back} to the newspaper club room.
{f:I|I} hoped nothing would happen during the fourth story...{p}

I see.
It's true that when you're healthy, you probably don't think people die all that easily.
Then let's shift the topic a little, toward life and death.{p}{a}{f:,|,} you get scared when you climb up somewhere high, don't you?
Yes
No

His name was Uehara, and he often bragged about how brave he was.
He'd sit at the window in dangerous poses; even in little everyday things, he loved to do something risky.
He was on the rugby team.
And on that team, something like this happened.
"If you jump off the roof and live, I'll make you a starter on the spot."
That's what an upperclassman on the rugby team said to the new members.
Of course, he must have figured no one would ever do it.
The juniors were stung.
"Hey, Uehara, you do it."
"Come on, you'd die, no matter what."
"Jumping off the roof isn't a question of guts or stamina.
You'd die for sure."{p}

"But it's galling, isn't it? Him saying that 'cause he thinks we can't do it."
Uehara listened to their talk in silence.
Of course, both the upperclassman and Uehara's friends had only said it as a joke.
No one would ever actually do such a thing.
But from then on, Uehara couldn't get the idea of jumping off the roof out of his head.
(Would I really die for sure?)
Uehara couldn't stop wondering about it.
Whenever he had a spare moment, he started going to the roof to look down at the ground.{p}

One time, he climbed over the railing and went outside it.
Outside the railing, there was a ledge only a dozen or so centimeters wide.
"Whoaaa, this feels amazing!"
Uehara felt a thrill he had never known before.
After that, he often went out past the railing on the roof.{p}

"Announcing the starters.........."
The rugby team's starters were announced.
"Uehara, ......."
He had made the starting lineup as a first-year.
"Uehara, you earned that spot on your own merit.
So quit going up to the roof now."
"Oh... okay."
Everyone on the team laughed.
But Uehara didn't stop going up to the roof.{p}

Then one day, a corpse was found in the water tank on the roof, and the roof was off-limits for a while.
Uehara was dying to go up there.{p}

One night, he finally snuck into the school and went up to the roof.
After so long, the roof felt exhilarating.
Then he climbed over the railing and stepped outside it.
"I want to stay here forever."
Uehara murmured that to himself.{p}

And then he quietly stood up and jumped.
It was an exhilaration unlike anything he had ever felt.
And as he felt death, he realized it clearly:
he had wanted to die all along.{p}

He died.
If you jump off the roof of the new school building, you die.
That's why he liked being on the roof, you see.
Feeling death was a joy to him.
After that incident, the roof was off-limits for a while.
But why don't you try sneaking up there sometime?
I hear Uehara is there.
They say he jumps off the roof every night.
And when someone comes, they say Uehara tells them this:
"Let's jump together."{p}And that's the end of my story.
Next, please.{p}

This time, rather than fear, I'd like to tell you about someone who had little sense of the worth of life.
Though high schoolers these days seem to lean that way a bit, too.
They say it's because, with nuclear families and housing conditions and so on, many people have never seen a relative or a pet die up close.
That's why so many juvenile crimes lately are so cruel, or so the story goes.
People actually die surprisingly easily, though.
I used to be the same as you, {a}{f:,|,} and never gave death a thought.
But the incident I'm about to tell you made me start thinking about life.{p}

There was a student who could kill the animals in the school's animal hutch without batting an eye.
Each time, a teacher scolded him, but the lectures were all appeals to his feelings, so the scolding made no sense to him at all.
"Morikawa, don't you feel sorry for them?"
"Sorry about that."
To him, it felt like no more than breaking some school equipment.
"You eat meat and fish yourself, don't you? Then quit eating it."
He looked like he wanted to say something like that.
Even on his way home, if he came across a small animal within easy reach, he would torment it to death.{p}

Then one day, Yoko Nakayama, a girl in his class, brought her pet hamster to school.
"Yoko, it's so cute!"
"You'll be in big trouble if the teacher finds out."
"Let's all keep it safe."
Everyone doted on the hamster.{p}
But when Morikawa saw that hamster, he wanted to torment it.{p}

At first, he held back.
"Come on, it's Nakayama's pet, after all."
But holding back only made the urge grow stronger.
Morikawa waited for his chance.
Third period ended.{p}

Several girls gathered around Nakayama.
"Next is P.E."
"Yoko, what are you going to do with the hamster?"
"It'll be fine. It'll stay quiet in my bag for an hour or so."
Talking like that, they headed off to the changing room.{p}

The classroom was dead silent; faint voices drifted in from the class next door.
After making sure there was no one in the hallway, Morikawa went over to Nakayama's desk.{p}

Then he opened her bag and took out the hamster.
He tormented it mercilessly until it was dead.{p}What do you think he did with the hamster after that?
He threw it in the trash
He put it back in the bag

When he got back, Nakayama's class was in an uproar.
Of course, Morikawa knew why, but he asked,
"What's going on?"
just the same.
"Nakayama's hamster's gone missing."
"Everyone, let's help look for it."
Someone suggested that, so they started searching.
"It's not here. Maybe it got out of the room."
"Guys, the teacher's coming!"
When someone said that, everyone stopped searching.{p}

But the hamster wasn't found, and school let out.
"Where could my hamster have gone?"
Nakayama said, worried.
"Let's do the cleaning.
If we look while we clean, I'm sure we'll find it."
The girl on cleaning duty with her that day tried to cheer her up.{p}

As everyone else went home, a few stayed behind to start cleaning, and Morikawa was among them.
(Crap. I've gotta hurry and get rid of the hamster in the trash can.)
Thinking that, he casually went to get the trash can.
"Yoko, I'll take the trash out to the incinerator."
He'd been beaten to it.
"Yoshioka, I'll go, so you help her look for the hamster."
"Oh, thanks."
With that, Morikawa took over taking out the trash.{p}

Morikawa picked up the trash can and headed for the incinerator.
When he got there, he tossed in the trash and the hamster.
Then he piled trash over the hamster.
(That should do it.)
Just as he thought that and turned to head back to the classroom...{p}

"So it was you after all."
It was Nakayama.
"To think it really was killed..."
"It's not like that.
I thought you'd be sad if you found out it was dead..."
"Liar!"{p}What do you think Morikawa did then?
He kept up the lie
He told her the truth
He ran away

That's right, he kept up the lie.
"I don't know anything about it.
I just thought you'd be sad if I showed it to you."
That's what Morikawa said.
Nakayama ran to the hamster and held it in her arms.
He walked away from there.{p}

From the next day on, Nakayama stopped coming to school.
Morikawa was racked with guilt, but
"It's just a little animal that cost a few hundred yen,"
he told himself as an excuse, or so I heard.{p}

Some time later, when he'd almost forgotten about it, Nakayama, who had been absent all that time, was waiting for Morikawa near his house.
"Long time no see."
"Nakayama..."
"Lately, I've started to understand how you feel.
Look..."{p}

Nakayama opened her bag, and inside were the carcasses of dozens of small animals.
"Well?"
Hamsters and other creatures, lots of them, lay dead with their eyes wide open.
The carcasses, which shouldn't have been seeing anything, seemed to be staring at Morikawa, accusing him.
Even Morikawa felt sick.
"Ugh... urk."
What was in his stomach slowly crept up his throat.{p}

That night, he had no appetite at all.
The sight of the carcasses Nakayama had shown him wouldn't leave his mind.
They say he didn't touch a bite of the hamburger steak he usually loved.
He went back to his room early and went straight to bed.
I wonder how long he had been asleep.
A noise woke him up.{p}

"Geez, I'm trying to sleep. Keep it down."
Thinking it was the TV, Morikawa went to the living room to complain.
The living room lights were off; it was pitch dark.
When he looked at the clock again, it was three in the morning.
(Nobody'd be watching TV at this hour.
...So what was that?){p}

This time, he could tell for certain that the noise was coming from inside his own house.
He moved forward, straining his ears.{p}

(Something's coming from this room...)
It was his parents' room.
(Are Mom and Dad still up?
What are they doing?){p}
...And there was Nakayama.{p}

In the darkness, something like a cord was moving.
"Nakayama... you...!"
She was strangling his parents with a rope.
"Oh my, I said I'd tell you next time, but you just couldn't wait...?
You know, it's the best, killing people.
With animals, you were my senior, but now I'm the one ahead.
Oh, that's right.
To thank you, I'll teach you how to kill a person.
Hee hee, hee... hee..."
Morikawa tried to lunge at Nakayama.{p}

At that moment, his murdered mother's head lolled over to face him.
"Ugh..."
His mother's face was twisted in agony, and her eyes looked terribly sad, they say.
...Morikawa passed out.{p}

The next day, when Morikawa didn't come to school, his teacher got worried and came to his house.
But no matter how many times the teacher rang the doorbell, no one answered.
There were traces of blood at the front door.
Thinking it strange, the teacher called the police, apparently.{p}

...Morikawa was in his parents' room.
They say he had laid his parents' bodies out neatly side by side, and was sitting next to them, staring blankly.
At first, Morikawa was investigated as a suspect, but he was soon cleared.
But he had become so unstable that he had to be put in a hospital.
Did they catch the killer, you ask?
No, not yet.
Morikawa said that Nakayama was the one who did it, but...
The police didn't believe him; they said it was a crime no girl could possibly commit.{p}

That's right, he told her the truth.
"But it's just a hamster.
They're not that expensive, right?
I'll pay you back for it sometime."
